intro.objective: Read, write and order whole numbers up to millions. Understand the value of each digit in a number. Compare integers using < and > and place them on a number line.
commonMistakes: Confusing the value of a digit with the digit itself — for example, the 3 in 35,000 is worth 30,000, not 3.
Forgetting that when comparing numbers with different numbers of digits, the one with more digits is larger.
Putting negative numbers in the wrong order — remember, −7 is less than −2.
Not lining up digits by place value when comparing — always start from the left.
methodSteps: Step 1: Identify the value of each digit by its position (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands…).
Step 2: To compare two numbers, start from the largest place value and work right.
Step 3: Use < (less than) or > (greater than) to show which is bigger.
Step 4: To order a set of numbers, compare pairs using Steps 2–3 and arrange them.
Step 5: Check your answer makes sense — read the numbers back in order.
workedExample: Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest: 4,502   4,520   4,052
Step 1 — Identify place values: All have 4 thousands.
Step 2 — Compare the hundreds: 4,052 has 0 hundreds; 4,502 and 4,520 both have 5 hundreds.
Step 3 — Compare the tens for the remaining two: 4,502 has 0 tens; 4,520 has 2 tens. So 4,502 < 4,520.

methodReminder: 1  Identify the value of each digit
2  Compare from the largest place value

questions.content:
Write down the value of the 6 in each of these numbers.

   a) 6,421       b) 3,602       c) 46,000       d) 609,000

Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest.

   8,304     8,034     8,340     8,403

Use < or > to make each statement correct.

   a) 12,500 ___ 12,050
   b) −3 ___ −8
   c) 99,999 ___ 100,000

A number has 5 digits. The ten-thousands digit is 7, the hundreds digit is 4, and all other digits are 0.

Write down the number.

Here are five number cards:  3   0   7   5   2

Using each card exactly once, make:
   a) the largest possible 5-digit number
   b) the smallest possible 5-digit number

The temperature at midnight was −4 °C. By noon it had risen by 11 degrees.

What was the temperature at noon?
Show your working.

Three towns have populations:
   Ashford: 125,400
   Bexley: 125,040
   Croydon: 152,400

   a) Write the towns in order of population, smallest first.
   b) The population of Ashford increases by 3,000. Is it now larger than Croydon? Explain your answer.

A six-digit number has these clues:
• The hundred-thousands digit is one more than the tens digit.
• The tens digit is 4.
• The number is between 500,000 and 600,000.
• The ones digit is half the hundreds digit.
• The hundreds digit is 8.
• The thousands and ten-thousands digits are both 0.

Find the number. Show how each clue helped you.

rows: Q7: a) Bexley, Ashford, Croydon  b) 125,400 + 3,000 = 128,400 — still less than 152,400, so no.
Q8: The number is 500,804. Hundred-thousands = 5 (one more than tens 4); tens = 4; hundreds = 8; ones = 4 (half of 8); thousands and ten-thousands = 0.
